parked.spanish: No serás detrás de muchos a males, y no responderás sobre contienda para inclinarte detrás de muchos para torcer.

findings.issue: Qal infinitive construct has no pronominal suffix; the reflexive clitic marks the addressee as the object of inclinar.
Hiphil infinitive of the same lemma is rendered torcer, a narrower twist, so the causative incline/turn is only partly visible.

parked.spanish: Cuando encuentras buey de tu enemigo o su asno errante, devolviendo lo devolverás a él.

findings.issue: The masculine singular participle follows the או pair; «asno errante» binds wandering only to the donkey and closes whether it also describes the ox.

parked.spanish: La fiesta de los panes ázimos guardarás; siete días comerás panes ázimos, conforme a lo que te mandé, al tiempo señalado del mes de las espigas, porque en él saliste desde Egipto; y no se verán mis faces vacío.

findings.issue: הָאָבִיב is singular; «las espigas» is plural.
פָנַי is a common noun; «faces» is English, not current Spanish.
רֵיקָם is an adverb; «vacío» is a masculine singular adjective and does not mark that adverb clearly.

parked.spanish: Tres veces en el año será visto todo tu varón a faces del señor Jehová.

findings.issue: «faces» is not current Spanish in this line; a reader must guess that it means face or presence.

readerNotes.note: Added "al" (a + el) before "malo" because Spanish requires an article on a substantivized adjective used as a direct object; no concept is added beyond the Hebrew's generic sense.

The Hebrew word order left in Spanish made 'su resto' read as subject; reordering with a resumptive 'lo' restores 'el animal del campo' as the one eating, per the 3fs verb's agreement with feminine חַיַּת.
«faces» is not current Spanish in this line; a reader must guess that it means face or presence.
Chose 'hasta la mañana' over bare 'hasta mañana' to keep בֹּקֶר as the noun morning rather than the adverb tomorrow.
Chose the causative-passive construction 'no se te hará servirlos' over an active rendering so the Spanish verb matches the Hophal stem rather than qal.
Chose 'junco' (rush) over 'caña' (reed) as the licensed rendering of סוּף; both are grammatically valid lexical options for this common noun.
